seoTitle: How to Change or Revise Buyer Feedback on eBay in 2025
metaDescription: Learn how buyers and sellers can revise feedback on eBay, including sending a revision request from Seller Hub and the time limits that apply.
intro: A piece of feedback left in a hurry, before an issue got resolved, can follow an eBay account for a long time — and eBay only gives both sides a narrow, rule-bound window to fix it. This guide covers the process from both directions: how a buyer responds when a seller asks for a revision, and how a seller sends that request in the first place after sorting out a shipping delay or a dispute. It also walks through where your feedback numbers actually live in the account, since that's the part most people never look at until they need to.

steps.heading: Find your feedback profile and revision requests
steps.body: Your feedback profile is the page that tallies everything: positive, neutral, and negative ratings broken out by the last 1, 6, and 12 months, plus a separate box for detailed seller ratings once you've crossed 10 of them. The number that matters most for this guide sits just above the feedback table itself — "Feedback revision requests available," a small counter that shows how many revision requests you have left to send. eBay caps this, so it's worth checking before you assume you can just ask again on the next order.

image.caption: A feedback profile showing zero ratings so far, with the revision-requests-available counter visible above the feedback list.

steps.heading: Understand what a feedback profile page shows
steps.body: eBay's own help documentation breaks down what's visible on any member's feedback profile: overall score, percentage positive, recent comments and photos, detailed seller ratings, and the date they registered. It's the same page whether you're checking your own history or a seller's before you buy from them. One detail worth knowing — reach a feedback score of 10 and you get a colored star badge on your profile, climbing all the way to a silver shooting star past a million, which is eBay's way of signaling account trustworthiness at a glance.

image.caption: eBay's Help Center page explaining what a feedback profile displays, including the star-rating milestones tied to feedback score.

steps.heading: As a buyer, respond to a revision request
steps.body: If a seller resolves an issue after you've already left feedback, they can send you a formal revision request rather than just messaging you directly. That request shows up with a prompt to either update the star rating and comment you originally left, or decline and keep it as-is. Read it before responding — you're not obligated to change anything, but if the seller genuinely fixed the problem (reshipped an item, issued a refund, cleared up a miscommunication), updating the feedback keeps your own history accurate.

steps.heading: As a seller, send a feedback revision request through Seller Hub
steps.body: Sellers initiate this from Seller Hub rather than the feedback page itself. Locate the order tied to the feedback you want revisited, and use the revision request option attached to that transaction. This only makes sense after you've actually resolved whatever prompted the negative or neutral rating — sending a request before the issue is fixed just wastes one of your limited requests and rarely changes the buyer's mind.

steps.heading: Check your purchases for feedback you still owe
steps.body: The flip side of revision requests is feedback you haven't left yet. My eBay's Purchases tab filters orders by status, and one of those filters is "Ready for feedback" — a quick way to see which completed orders are still waiting on your review. Clearing this out regularly means you're less likely to leave a rushed, low-effort rating days later that you end up wanting to revise.

image.caption: The My eBay Purchases page, with a "Ready for feedback" filter alongside Processing, Unpaid items, and Returns & Canceled.

steps.heading: Know eBay's time limits and revision caps
steps.body: eBay doesn't allow unlimited do-overs. Revision requests have to be sent within a set window after the original feedback was left, and each account only gets a handful of requests over a rolling period — the exact count is shown right on your feedback profile, as covered in step one. Once that window closes or the count hits zero, the feedback is effectively locked in, so it's worth acting as soon as an issue is actually resolved rather than sitting on it.

steps.heading: Know what happens if no one responds
steps.body: A revision request doesn't revise anything on its own — it's an invitation, not an automatic change. If the buyer never opens it or lets the response window lapse, the original feedback stays exactly as it was written. That's worth keeping in mind on both sides: buyers shouldn't assume ignoring a request makes it go away quietly, and sellers shouldn't assume sending one guarantees a better rating.

faq.question: Can a seller ask me to change feedback I already left?
faq.answer: Yes, sellers can send a feedback revision request through Seller Hub, which buyers can then choose to accept or ignore.

faq.question: Is there a time limit to revise feedback on eBay?
faq.answer: Yes, eBay only allows feedback revisions within a limited time window and caps how many revision requests an account can send, shown as a counter right on the feedback profile page.

faq.question: What happens if I don't respond to a revision request?
faq.answer: If no action is taken within the allowed time, the original feedback generally remains unchanged.

faq.question: Can sellers change feedback on their own without buyer approval?
faq.answer: No, sellers can only request a revision; the buyer has to approve the change for it to take effect.

faq.question: Where do I see if I still owe a buyer feedback?
faq.answer: Open My eBay, go to Purchases, and use the "Ready for feedback" filter to see which completed orders you haven't rated yet.
